Design System

Every specimen below is rendered with the application's real compiled stylesheet and its real class names — this page inlines src/index.css rather than reproducing it, so nothing here can drift from what ships. Token values in the tables are read live from the browser with getComputedStyle, meaning they are the true resolved values, not transcriptions.

Regenerate with npm run styleguide. Written reference and usage guidance live in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md.

Colour

The identity is a deep maroon that carries every primary action and every "you are here" signal — it should stay rare enough to mean something. Everything else is a supporting neutral or a status ramp.

Brand
Surfaces
Text

Accessibility: --color-text-faint on white falls below WCAG AA for body text. It is fine for placeholders and decoration — never put information there that exists nowhere else.

Borders
Status ramps
Domain — record type & outcome

Colour is never the only signal — every status above is also carried by text or an icon. Roughly 1 in 12 readers cannot rely on the green/amber/red distinction.

Typography

The serif is doing real work: it marks scholarly content — a paper title, an APA reference, a pulled quote — as distinct from interface chrome. Never use it for buttons, labels or navigation.

Families
TokenSpecimenUse for
--font-display Replication Atlas Titles, citations, quoted material, KPI values
--font-body Replication Atlas Everything else — all interface text
--font-mono 10.1037/xge0001234 DOIs, identifiers, code, keyboard keys
Size ramp
TokenSizeSpecimenUse for

This ramp overrides Tailwind's defaults — text-sm is 12px here, not 14px. That is deliberate: it is what makes two separate apps built on this system look like siblings.

Weight & leading
TokenSpecimenUse for
--font-weight-normalBody copy and valuesParagraphs, data values
--font-weight-mediumMildly emphasised UISecondary buttons, chips
--font-weight-semiboldThe workhorse weightButtons, tabs, list titles, active states
--font-weight-boldDisplay and badgesTitles, uppercase badges
--leading-snugHeadings and clamped list-item titles use tighter leading.Headings, list titles
--leading-looseLong-form body copy is set looser so it stays readable across full lines.Paragraphs (the body default)

Avoid weight 400 below 12px — it disappears. Anything at --text-2xs should be uppercase, semibold and tracked.

Spacing

A 4px grid. Gaps inside a component come from steps 1–2; padding of a component from 3–4; gaps between components from 4–6. If you want something between two steps, you almost certainly want one of the two steps.

TokenValueScaleUse for

Radius & borders

Radius should grow with the element. A 6px control inside a 10px card inside a 14px dialog reads as intentional; the same radius at all three sizes does not.

Border widths
TokenValueSpecimenUse for

Elevation

A ladder, not a grab-bag — pick by how far the surface floats above the page. --shadow-chrome is not "between sm and md"; it is a different job, for fixed chrome sitting directly on the page rather than on a card.

Focus rings — never remove without replacing

Motion

Fast and understated. Nothing that blocks interaction should exceed 200ms. Hover the swatches to feel each duration.

Easing: --ease-standard by default, --ease-out for entering elements, --ease-emphasized for modal pop-in, and --ease-spring for the toast's slight overshoot. Animate opacity and transform where you can.

Breakpoints

Direction matters. Tailwind variants are min-width (lg: means 960px and up), while the hand-written CSS in this app is desktop-first and uses the same numbers as max-width. Both are legitimate — just don't mix them inside one component.

TokenValueWhat changes

The 960px boundary additionally splits on orientation: landscape keeps a shortened sidebar, portrait flattens to one scrolling column. That is specific to this app's split-pane layout, not a general system rule.

Buttons

Note the hover convention: filled buttons darken, while ghost and outline controls signal interactivity by adopting the brand colour rather than changing their fill.

Chips & filters

Chips are interactive and stateful — that is what separates them from badges. Active state is always a maroon tint plus a maroon border, never a fill.

Chrome is dark so content reads as the figure and navigation as the ground. Active tabs are marked with brand colour plus a 2px rule — colour alone would not survive a greyscale print.

Toasts

Bottom-right, stacked, auto-dismissing after 5 seconds. The 4px left edge carries the status colour; the icon repeats it so the meaning survives without colour. Toasts are for things the user does not need to act on — anything requiring a decision is a dialog.

Alert dialogs

Centred, blurred backdrop, single confirming action. Use these only when the user must acknowledge something before continuing — if they can safely ignore it, use a toast.

Modals

Width is chosen by content, not importance — 420px for a confirm, 920px for a chart. Every modal is a column: fixed header, scrolling body, fixed footer, with actions bottom-right.
